cells.findings: capacity-blind by design: distributes evenly across all three targets regardless of service time.
reacts to in-flight count: should favor the two fast targets once the slow target's backlog grows.
reacts to observed latency: should favor the two fast targets once each has been sampled at least once.
randomized pairwise comparison over load: should also favor the fast targets, with a fixed seed here only to confirm it runs under virtual time -- 005-F is the dedicated seed-reproducibility proof.

findings: All four policies ran 300 requests over a fixed, deterministic arrival schedule (no wall-clock, no real goroutines) against one slow (100ms) and two fast (20ms) targets. Round Robin split evenly across all three regardless of speed; Least Connections, EWMA, and P2C-over-load all shifted traffic toward the two fast targets once they had something to react to -- reproducing Stage 3's own qualitative routing findings, now under a fully virtual clock.
